title: Risk Appetite
summary: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk an organisation is willing to accept while pursuing its objectives, and it is a decision made by leadership rather than by the security team alone. It is usually expressed as a statement plus tolerances, for example which data classes may be processed on a public cloud, how long a critical service may stay down, or how many high severity findings may remain open at quarter end. In a real environment it appears in the risk register, in exception approvals, and in the trade offs made when a deadline competes with a control. The frequent mistake is to write a broad statement such as low appetite for risk and never convert it into thresholds, so every argument about a finding becomes a matter of opinion instead of a comparison against an agreed line.

beginner.definition: Risk appetite is the level of risk a company is willing to accept to reach its goals. It is a choice made by leaders, not by the security team alone. It is written down so that everyone can use the same limit. Below that limit a risk is accepted, and above it someone must act.
beginner.whyItMatters: Without a stated limit, every risk decision becomes an argument. One team wants to fix everything, and another wants to ship the product. Leaders may not know which risks they are carrying. A clear appetite lets people decide faster and defend the choice. It also shows customers and regulators that risks are managed on purpose.
howItWorks: Leaders agree on the goals of the business and the level of harm they can accept.
They write the appetite as a short statement, then add measurable tolerances for key areas.
Teams compare each real risk against those tolerances during normal planning work.
Risks above the line need treatment, and risks below it are recorded and reviewed.
Exceptions are approved with an owner and an end date, never left open forever.
Leaders review the appetite each year, because the business and the threats change.
beginner.example: Think of a family that is buying a house together. They agree in advance how much debt feels safe each month. That agreed number is what risk appetite means in practice. When a bigger house appears, they check the payment against the limit. A deal above the limit needs a plan, such as a smaller loan. A deal below the limit can go ahead with a note in the file.
takeaways: Risk appetite is a leadership decision, and it must be written as limits.
A statement without numbers cannot settle an argument about a finding.
Every exception needs a named owner and a date when it ends.

objectives: Explain what risk appetite means and who is responsible for setting it.
Describe how a risk appetite statement is turned into measurable tolerances.
Explain how tolerances guide the treatment of findings and the approval of exceptions.
Recognise the failure mode of a broad statement that contains no thresholds.
Outline why risk appetite is reviewed as the business and the threats change.
